findings.reason: the §7 node has no band to leave and would either invent a threshold or report an unmeasurable clause, so the plan must state §7's own per-code failure threshold against the generating state.
findings.text: §7 clause (3) states "the size at which the axis position and q95 first leave the §2 bands", but this review's s2 change makes the ITER row exempt: §2 now reads "The ITER row is reported against the same measures under the label same magnetics, different constraints and is not judged against the bands" (snapshot:124), and §7's only case is ITER, so the clause names a threshold that does not apply to the row it measures — additionally, §2's bands are nova-versus-imas-efit agreement measures, while §7's error is against the held generating state, so even a non-exempt row would not give the clause a defined threshold

findings.reason: a reader of §7 will compare the two columns as equal-constraint estimates, so the plan must carry that §2 label into §7's table and state that the per-code drift measures are not a like-for-like code comparison on ITER.
findings.text: §7 presents the two codes as reconstructing "both sequences from the same rows" and reports per-code drift and band exit beside EFIT, while the same commit's s2 change records that on ITER the two codes do not share a constraint set ("imas-efit's ITER reconstruction also carries a synthesised on-axis pressure point and a q0 prior that the class does not", snapshot:107), and the c-s2-iter-priors ruling says the gap is read before any prior is added or a prior-free imas-efit run is requested; §7's only stated handling is to read imas-efit's configuration back and report it, which does not stop the drift table being read as a like-for-like comparison

findings.reason: an unmeasured prerequisite inside the comparison section makes §7's single done-when unreviewable and its effort wrong, so the EFIT execution path needs its own section or a named prerequisite node.
findings.text: the locked `efit-on-synthetic-rows` choice makes §7 deliver both the drift study and a new capability, "a nova node builds and runs imas-efit on the synthetic noisy rows" with nova owning the EFIT configuration, whose cost the decision's own context states ("Running it from nova needs imas-efit's entry point to accept an ITER magnetics-only case built by nova", snapshot:199); no section delivers or gates that path, and §7 keeps its 8 h and its single implemented status, so its gate can fail on the imas-efit wiring while the drift measurement is sound, or vice versa
